biography.plain_text: Adam Katz is an American real estate developer, attorney and pilot who founded the Long Island charter operator Talon Air. After building a career managing and investing in New York property, he launched the aviation company with his own aircraft fleet and flew in regular rotation. He later sold Talon while retaining separate development interests.

confidence.reason: The direct profile, Forbes, Business Jet Traveler and Times Union jointly establish Katz's property career, legal and flying qualifications, founding and operating role, personal flight rotation, 2018 sale and retained separate development interests.

long_biography.plain_text:
Adam Katz brought a pilot's perspective to Talon Air, the Long Island charter company he founded. He had earned commercial, instrument and instructor qualifications before establishing an aviation operation designed around direct control of aircraft, crews and service.

At Republic Airport, Katz assembled a modern jet fleet and developed a purpose-built hangar. He continued flying as a captain and instructor while expanding Talon beyond charter into aircraft management, maintenance and fixed-base services. The company's operating model combined technical oversight with tailored travel for private clients, supported by the facilities and staff to manage each aircraft in house.

uncertainties.detail: Adam Katz is a common name. The dedicated Forbes profile and Wikipedia page belong to a Wasserman baseball agent educated at Dickinson and Notre Dame; they are rejected. Person ID 2755 instead resolves to the New York property developer and Talon Air founder through the immutable Kashmir relationship, YachtBuyer's owner attribution, Great Neck and Farmingdale geography, Roxann, Talon and professional-pilot anchors.

Katz sold Talon Air in 2018, so Founder and Operator cannot be used as current aviation relationships. Public records show retained development interests and recent Stratosphere continuity, but do not establish his present principal asset, portfolio scale or a current controlling operating mandate over the main wealth source. Real Estate is therefore used as the required origin-sector fallback, while wealth relationship remains Unknown; Operator and Founder are preserved only as strongest historical alternatives.

Sources positively document Katz's own property transactions, development work and Talon Air founding, supporting broad Self-made classification. The comptroller decision's reference to the Katz family owning and operating properties does not identify a predecessor, transfer, inherited company, inherited stake or succession event, so it is not treated as inheritance evidence. Starting capital and family financial circumstances remain undisclosed.

The most detailed Roxann property biography is older, while recent aggregated corporate records show Stratosphere active with Katz as a member but do not enumerate his current portfolio or day-to-day duties. The Property developer tag is therefore former-but-defining rather than current. Real Estate remains the primary-industry origin fallback without claiming unsupported present scale.

Katz's direct profile and Business Jet Traveler date Talon Air's founding to 2001, while a later interview with the post-acquisition chief executive describes the company as founded in 1999. The dossier uses 2001 because it is tied directly to Katz's commercial-pilot progression and is repeated by exact-founder sources; the discrepancy does not affect the 2018 sale or historical Founder classification.

The owner input links Katz to historical Kashmir and current Seaquel, while YachtBuyer independently names Adam Katz in Kashmir's rebuild. That context is used only to resolve identity. No vessel, dimension, ownership date or ownership claim appears in the biographies or wealth classifications.

The direct profile establishes that Katz grew up in New York City and Great Neck but does not establish a precise birthplace or birth date. No strong exact-person source reviewed established a middle name, secondary nationality or secondary residence, so those fields remain blank.

No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or website cleared the common-name identity threshold. Talon Air's company website is not proposed because Katz sold the business, and the Forbes and Wikipedia profiles belong to the sports agent.

Only approved active tags are proposed. Property developer, Aviation and Pilot each meet an existing semantic contract; more granular private-charter, aircraft-management and aviation-entrepreneur concepts are inactive and remain ordinary research facts rather than new candidates.
